paragraphs: A transformer is the neural network design behind most modern language models. Its key trick is attention: for every word it is processing, the model scores how relevant every other word in the passage is, then blends the most relevant ones into its understanding of that word.

Older designs read text one word at a time, in order, and tended to forget the start of long passages. Transformers look at the whole passage at once, which makes them far easier to train on huge amounts of text in parallel. That is a large part of why models got so much bigger and better after 2017, when the design was introduced.
